_about: The platform's one timeline (the product owner's decisions of 2026-10-22): every future hazard dataset and every pathway-year is placed by the global warming it represents, in °C above 1995–2014. Read only by services/reference/warming_axis.py; no warming number is typed anywhere in the code (tests/unit/test_warming_axis.py).

choices: one timeline for every future hazard: the warming level, not calendar periods
the warming comes from the IPCC AR6 assessment, not from the platform's own four-model CMIP6 set (which runs warmer: SSP5-8.5 2081–2100 +4.65 °C against the assessed +3.5 °C above 1995–2014)
a level is a 20-year average — the length of every modelled period
a pathway-year reads any dataset at that warming, whatever pathway made it
between two datasets the hazard is blended by warming, then the damage curve applied
warmer than every dataset: a named gap, never extrapolated

baseline.basis: the reference period of the platform's modelled changes (scripts/build_cmip6_global.py HIST) and of the IPCC AR6 projections

assessed.dataset: IPCC AR6 WG1 Summary for Policymakers — data for Figure SPM.8 (v20210809), panel (a)
assessed.citation: Fyfe, J.; Fox-Kemper, B.; Kopp, R.; Garner, G. (2021): Summary for Policymakers of the Working Group I Contribution to the IPCC Sixth Assessment Report - data for Figure SPM.8 (v20210809). NERC EDS Centre for Environmental Data Analysis. doi:10.5285/98af2184e13e4b91893ab72f301790db
assessed.describes: 'Global Surface Air Temperature (GSAT) anomalies relative to 1850-1900 (20 year means)'; 'These changes were obtained by combining CMIP6 model simulations with observational constraints … as well as an updated assessment of equilibrium climate sensitivity' (CEDA catalogue record)
assessed.rebase: 'Changes relative to 1850–1900 based on 20-year averaging periods are calculated by adding 0.85°C' (CEDA catalogue record): the series is moved to 1995–2014 by subtracting its own historical file's 1995–2014 mean, which the axis checks equals the stated offset to the stated precision
assessed.range: the 5–95% range of the assessment (its very likely range)
assessed.used_for: windows made from climate-model output — a future map, a modelled horizon — and the score lane's years

observed.dataset: HadCRUT5 analysis, global annual summary series (HadCRUT.5.0.2.0), Met Office Hadley Centre / Climatic Research Unit
observed.attribution: Contains public sector information licensed under the Open Government Licence v3.0 (HadCRUT.5.0.2.0, Met Office Hadley Centre and Climatic Research Unit, University of East Anglia)
observed.rebase: the file's anomalies are relative to 1961–1990; they are moved to 1995–2014 by subtracting the file's own 1995–2014 mean
observed.used_for: windows made from observations — a dataset's present day

pathways_basis: the platform's declared pathway ↔ SSP mapping, the one the score lane's modelled changes use (scripts/build_cmip6_global.py SSPS) and the flood maps' scenario basis states (RCP4.5 ↔ SSP2-4.5, RCP8.5 ↔ SSP5-8.5)
anchors_basis: the platform's horizons are these periods: the score lane's modelled changes average 2021–2040, 2041–2060 and 2081–2100 (scripts/build_cmip6_global.py PERIODS); 'current' is the platform's present year, its level the assessed 20-year average for that year

rules.year: a year's level is the assessed 20-year average the series gives for it, under the pathway asked
rules.window: the mean of the levels of its years; the assessed series ends in 2099, so a window running to 2100 is measured on its years to 2099
rules.made_from: a window made from observations is measured on the observed record; one made from climate-model output on the assessed series under its pathway
rules.placement: a pathway-year reads the two datasets whose levels bracket its own — the nearest at or below, the nearest above — weighted by how far its level lies between theirs
rules.beyond: a pathway-year warmer than every dataset of a hazard is a named gap; colder than its present day cannot occur for a future year and is refused
